transcript.text:
“Stopped working” can mean a few different things. The common simple causes are a flat/failed battery or power-supply issue, a blocked filter/air path making it overheat and cut out, or—if it is completely dead despite a sound power supply—a switch or motor fault. 1. Switch it off and unplug it (or remove the battery). Empty the bin and check the hose, floorhead and visible airways for a blockage. A blockage can make a vacuum overheat and stop.
2. Check the filters are not packed with dust. If they are washable, clean them only as the filter instructions allow and let them dry completely before refitting—never run it with a wet filter.
3. If it stopped during use and felt hot, leave it switched off for at least 30–60 minutes after clearing any blockage, then try again. If it restarts, overheating from restricted airflow is likely. Is it a cordless Hoover or one with a mains lead, and when you press power is it completely dead, or does it run but have little/no suction?
its got a long wire, plugs in the wall. its completely dead when i switch it on, no noise at all

A completely dead corded vacuum is more likely to have a supply fault than a failed motor: first the wall socket, plug fuse or cable; then the on/off switch or internal wiring. 1. Unplug the Hoover. Try a lamp or phone charger in the same wall socket. If that does not work, the socket/circuit is the issue rather than the vacuum. 2. With the Hoover still unplugged, inspect the full lead and plug for cuts, crushing, scorching, looseness or a bent pin. If there is any damage, do not use it—have the lead/plug repaired or replaced. 3. If the socket and lead look sound, open the plug fuse carrier and check the fuse only with the same rating marked on the old fuse or plug. Then try it again. A blown fuse that immediately blows again points to an internal fault, so stop using it. If the socket is live and a correct new fuse makes no difference, the likely next causes are the on/off switch, cable connection or thermal protection internally. That needs an appliance repair engineer rather than dismantling it at home.
the lamp works in the socket. theres black tape on the wire near the plug, my son did it ages ago, its a bit bent there. I havent got a screwdriver or spare fuse

Do not plug or switch the vacuum on again. Tape is not a safe repair for a mains lead. The plug fuse could also have failed, but without a screwdriver and spare correct fuse there is no useful safe check left to do at home. Arrange for a vacuum-repair shop or suitably qualified electrician to inspect and replace the plug/lead as necessary. They should also check why the fuse failed before returning it to use. If the lead and plug prove sound, the next likely fault would be the vacuum’s on/off switch or internal wiring; that is also a repair-job rather than something to dismantle at home.
